title: Safety expert reveals lifesaving tip to 'gain advantage' on intruders
text:
By JANE HERZ, US SENIOR LIFESTYLE REPORTER

Updated:  06:04 AEST, 3 September 2026

A safety expert has revealed a lifesaving tip that could help you 'gain advantage' on an intruder if they break into your home.

The crucial information was shared in a new TikTok video made by Kailee Billerbeck, who is known by her online moniker, @everydayarmor.

Billerbeck is a second degree, level three black belt and the founder of self-defense program Everyday Armor, which teaches women how to defend themselves.

On her TikTok account, she often posts safety tips and practical advice for her followers.

In the new clip, she explained that if a stranger breaks into your house, the first thing that you want to do is run, but if that's not an option for you, there are many things you can do to protect yourself.

And according to Billerbeck, a simple tactic could help you get an edge: not turning on the lights.

'You need to immediately try to hide, but while you're doing this, do not turn on the lights,' Billerbeck urged in the video.

She explained that by turning on the lights, it can show the intruder where you are – plus, you know the layout of your house better than they do and can move around easier in the dark.

Safety expert Kailee Billerbeck has revealed a lifesaving tip that could help you 'gain advantage' on an intruder if they break into your home

Billerbeck recommended barricading yourself in a secure spot if someone breaks into your home.

'When you go to hide, you want to make sure that you are barricading yourself,' she said.

'Stack any kind of furniture you can to make it harder for them to get in, then hide behind something.'

'That's when you're going to then call emergency services,' she went on. 'If you can, call and leave the line open.'

The self-defense expert added that if you can't make a phone call, some areas allow you to text 911.

'Text them, let them know what's happening, let them know the address, the status update and explain the assailant if you know who it is,' she suggested.

If possible, Billerbeck said you should also grab something that could help you defend yourself just in case you end up coming face-to-face with the intruder.

She said that when looking for items, it's important to choose something that can increase your wingspan.

'You need to immediately try to hide, but while you're doing this, do not turn on the lights,' Billerbeck urged in the video

She also recommended barricading yourself in a secure spot if someone breaks into your home

She explained that by turning on the lights, it can show the intruder where you are - plus, you know the layout of your house better than they do and can move around easier in the dark (stock image)

'Often in fight or flight, you lose your fine motor skills and rely on large, sweeping movements, so look for things that increase your wingspan,' she said.

These items can be things like a lamp or even a baseball bat.

'Anything that's going to give you a little bit more reach and make an impact a little bit harder,' Billerbeck shared.

'You can swing for the side of the head to try to knock them out, sometimes it can be lethal, so obviously, only use this in self-defense,' she added.

Once you know it's safe to come out and you are sure that the intruder has left, Billerbeck warned viewers not to touch anything, and instead, try to document what went on.

Statistically, most home break-ins occur between 10am and 3pm, according to ADT.

Burglaries occur more often in the summer months rather than the winter months, with most targeting cash, expensive accessories and even prescription drugs.
